propositions: A runaway/truncated completion-verifier run is incorrectly disposed as a blocking FAIL (exit 1) instead of the retryable INDETERMINATE fault (exit 11) the contract requires when evidence is incomplete due to truncation.

In _restamp_marker echo branch, an un-banked met=false criterion (entry is None) has its insufficiency marker popped, creating a bare met=false indistinguishable from a genuine refutation, whereas the omitted-criterion branch correctly marks un-banked criteria insufficient.

The close_precheck and verify-completion verb only route to retryable exit 11 when verdict_obtainable is False, but not when evidence_sufficient is False, so insufficiency-only FAILs hard-block despite the reconciler deriving evidence_sufficient=False.
Fix A stamps un-banked met=false echoes (entry is None) with evidence_sufficient=False while preserving bare met=false for genuine refutations (present markerless entries).

Fix B introduces shared helper completion_fail_returncode() returning exit 11 when verdict_obtainable=False OR evidence_sufficient=False, ensuring both close_precheck and verify-completion have identical insufficiency disposition.
The runaway read_file guard itself fires correctly; the defect is downstream handling of truncated verdicts, introduced in commit 6b318ffaec4a (ticket 1d71-a76c-04f6-4642).
